architect-sketch-00.why: 'Caller's view' section precedes the type sketch: guard 'calls acquire once' and maps limited to 429.
Compares a 'Redis-backed HTTP middleware' with a single acquire operation and picks the latter because it 'keeps quota policy in one place'.
Exposes only createApiKeyRateLimiter returning AcquireApiKeyPermit; 'The module owns the key format, window bookkeeping, and expiry.'
'All four use the same Redis deployment' and refuses 'an instance-local quota, which would break the shared limit.'

architect-sketch-01.why: 'After authentication, call checkRateLimit(redis, apiKeyId) once per request' with 429/503 mapping.
Only alternative is 'A fixed-minute Redis counter', an algorithm variant behind the same API, not a structurally different design.
Single function checkRateLimit; 'Keep the limit, Redis key format, and window bookkeeping private.'
One atomic Redis operation 'so concurrent requests across all four instances share one quota', failing closed rather than relaxing the limit.

architect-sketch-02.why: 'Caller flow' describes passing Redis to createRateLimiter at startup and calling consume after auth.
Only contrasts fixed-window vs rolling-window counting, which it says stays 'out of the API contract' - not structurally different shapes.
createRateLimiter returns one consume method; Redis is bound once at startup.
'Redis is the shared source of truth... rather than falling back to independent per-instance quotas.'

architect-sketch-03.why: 'Caller's view' section shows consume use and 429/503 handling before the shape.
Rejects a fixed-window counter and 'A separate check / record API [that] would also expose a race between instances', choosing single consume.
createRateLimiter returns a single ConsumeRateLimit; 'callers only see the consume operation.'
'an API key gets 100 requests total, not 100 per instance' and 'Don't fall back to a per-instance quota.'

architect-sketch-04.why: 'Caller usage' covers startup, middleware passing the verified ID, and 429/503.
Alternative is 'middleware that owns the policy and calls a Redis counter module', rejected because it 'would also expose window and expiry details to the middleware'.
Single RateLimiter function type; 'Redis is visible at startup but not to request handlers.'
Middleware 'does not fall back to per-instance counters, which would break the shared limit.'

architect-sketch-05.why: 'Caller flow' describes calling checkRateLimit(redis, apiKeyId) and mapping results to 429/503.
Alternatives are only fixed-window vs sliding-window algorithms with the same contract, not structurally different designs.
One checkRateLimit function; 'keep the Redis details private to this one module.'
Says 'shared across all four instances. Redis is the source of truth' but never ties Redis to the multi-instance need or contrasts it with an in-memory counter.

ketchup-00.why: 'Two things wait on you: whether to pin the Stripe SDK or update the webhook verifier, and whether to merge the login-test fix.'
'I'd keep the old SDK pinned for now... a wrong change could reject valid webhooks or weaken verification. The pin is reversible.'
Stripe: verifier change could reject valid webhooks; login: 'a fixed clock masks behavior that depends on time advancing.'
Plain words, no hashes, commands or test counts; even says 'every audited icon passed'.

ketchup-01.why: 'Two calls are waiting on you: whether to pin the Stripe SDK or update the webhook verifier, and whether to merge the login-test fix.'
'I'd pin the old SDK for now. The pin is reversible and delays the upgrade; changing the verifier before confirming the cause could reject valid webhooks.'
Both items carry a risk: rejected webhooks / delayed upgrade, and 'a fixed clock could mask a timing issue.'
Plain prose; only user-supplied PR numbers and counts, no hashes or commands.

ketchup-02.why: 'Two things need you: merge PR #311 and decide whether PR #312 should pin the old Stripe SDK or update the webhook verifier.'
'pin the old SDK for now. That defers the upgrade but avoids changing signature verification on a hunch.'
Stripe: defers the upgrade; login: 'Risk is low: the change is limited to the test clock.'
Plain words without hashes, commands or test-run counts.

ketchup-03.why: 'Two things need your call: whether to pin the old Stripe SDK or update the webhook verifier, and whether to merge the login-test fix.'
'I'd pin the old SDK for now... Pinning is reversible and delays the upgrade; a verifier regression could reject valid webhooks.'
Each item has a risk, e.g. 'clock pinning masks a timing issue the test should catch.'
Plain words; no hashes, commands or extraneous test counts.

ketchup-04.why: 'Two calls are waiting on you: merge PR #311 and decide whether PR #312 should pin the old Stripe SDK or update the webhook verifier.'
Picks 'Pin the old SDK for now' because 'Updating the verifier before confirming the cause risks rejecting valid webhooks', with a plan to revisit the bump.
Stripe: risk of rejecting valid webhooks; login: 'Risk is low: pinning the clock... doesn't exercise behavior at other times.'
Plain words; no hashes or commands.

ketchup-05.why: 'Two calls need you: merge PR #311 and decide how to handle the Stripe SDK bump in PR #312.'
Gives a conditional answer ('update the verifier if the header change is confirmed... If it isn't confirmed, keep the old SDK pinned') without weighing pin's cost or committing to a pick.
#312: 'The risk is rejecting valid webhooks'; #311: 'Low risk: the fixed-clock test no longer exercises behavior as time advances.'
Plain words; no hashes or commands.

principles-new-requirement-00.why: Explicitly rejects a single status type and models payment and fulfillment as independent states, so 'shipped but unpaid' stays representable; no type given.
'I'd skip isRefunded and the compatibility adapter' and 'remove the old fields and callers in the same change.'
'Inventory reads and writes with a rerunnable search or AST check... then codemod only the patterns whose meaning is clear.'

principles-new-requirement-01.why: OrderState is two independent fields, so { paymentStatus: 'unpaid', fulfillmentStatus: 'shipped' } is representable.
'Don't add isRefunded or a permanent adapter... Migrate them by intent in one wave, then delete the old fields.'

principles-new-requirement-02.why: Union type excludes unpaid+shipped: '{ payment: 'unpaid'; shipment: 'not_shipped' } | { payment: 'paid' | 'refunded'; ... }', with transitions in one module.
'Don't add isRefunded or an adapter' and 'Migrate all 30 callers in the same change', making the check fail on legacy access.
'Use a rerunnable, type-aware check to inventory the reads and writes... automate the unambiguous rewrites.'

principles-new-requirement-03.why: Order type is two independent fields, leaving 'unpaid' + 'shipped' representable.
'I'd skip isRefunded and the adapter' and 'Migrate the callers and delete the old fields in the same change.'
'Use TypeScript's Find All References to inventory the reads and writes' plus a CI check against retired fields.

principles-new-requirement-04.why: Union '{ kind: "unpaid" } | { kind: "paid" | "refunded"; fulfillment: ... }' makes shipped-unpaid and refunded-unpaid unrepresentable.
'Don't add isRefunded or a compatibility adapter' and 'Migrate the ~30 callers and delete the flags in the same change.'
'use a rerunnable codemod for unambiguous cases. Use compiler errors to find the rest.'

principles-new-requirement-05.why: Union type with unpaid only unshipped; notes 'Three booleans... allow contradictions'.
'Don't add isRefunded or keep a compatibility adapter' and 'remove the old fields in the same migration.'
'Use compiler errors and a repository search to inventory callers' plus 'a rerunnable check for remaining legacy field references.'
